story_text.value:
It’s my website where I host my arrangements of public domain music completely for free. Right now there are only arrangements for my instrument, tuba, but I’d love to add more instruments like ocarina or bassoon in the future. I started this because over the 10 years I have played tuba, I probably went through all free tuba resources on the internet multiple times and many pieces I wanted to play I did not even find for tuba.

I’m working completely alone on this, so to be honest with you: I got a lot of AI help. Basically the pipeline for getting a public domain piece onto my website is downloading a well scanned score from a library like IMSLP, then a couple of Claude subagents read through it bar by bar and write the tuba part from it. A script checks for clashes with the piano accompaniment and a separate Claude session proofreads the result against the scan. Then I play it through myself, look through the sheet music and double check weird passages with other sources on the internet. Most of the time there are maybe 2 errors left in a big piece like the Can-Can, so the subagents already do a great job!

The sheet music player is rendered by alphaTab. It had some bugs that I patched, at some point I want to send them the fixes so they can fix them in alphaTab itself too. I also got a recording feature, there I had a big problem with the piano accompaniment coming through the speaker and tried to subtract it from the recording, but it still doesn’t work too well sadly. Lately I rewrote my page turn logic to do half page turns, cause every musician knows how frustrating it is to not see the next notes until the page turns.

My big vision is a bit unrealistic, but I want to somehow host all public domain pieces there are for free for all instruments, so people don’t have to pay $20 anymore for some Danse macabre euphonium arrangement for example... Would love to know from the musicians here whether you like my current arrangements and if you have ideas for other pain points I can try to fix for free with my website?

Thanks!

title.value: Show HN: Syncopate – free sheet music with piano play-along

Hi HN, I built Mana, a family organizer: shared calendars, shopping lists, receipt scanners, meal planning, chores, and notes for the whole household, with a built-in AI assistant ("add milk and eggs," "plan dinners for the week") plus automations (e.g., milk goes back on the list before it runs out).

Additionally, you can connect Mana MCP to your Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini etc.

The goal is to eventually take the model calls and storage to local but that's work to be done.

Appreciate if there's any feedback. Thank you!

story_text.value:
Hey HN! I was playing around with the Kepler and TESS data last weekend when I hacked around a way to pixel-peep stars dimming periodically to potentially find new exoplanets with Codex.

I ended up running the engine to find an interesting signal in Kepler data that was uncatalogued with a dip repeating every 13.77 days around KIC 5689121, a red dwarf in Lyra about 970 light-years away. If it's a planet, it'd be roughly 2.5–3 times Earth's radius !

Funnily enough, this candidate is just 7.1 arcseconds from a much brighter neighbour (KIC 5689116) and is very hard to see because of how much brighter it is (probably why it went unnoticed for so long)

Of course, there's work to do before calling it confirmed - my TRICERATOPS analysis is about 6.9% and we have to get IR/AO / Keck observations to prove it's out there ! (which I'm honestly intimidated by but cautiously optimistic about because I've never worked in non-CS adjacent research) but I found the activity of making cool tools to potentially discover things about our universe quite fun !

Would love feedback, especially from anyone who's worked with Kepler data or exoplanet validation :)

https://x.com/kuberwastaken/status/2109240782368751834

story_text.value:
Each round you get a spectrum with a target on it (Calm ----X-- Stressful). Name something that sits at the target: a job interview, a walk in the park, a goose?

The closer you are, the higher your score.

Mechanically it's like a crossover between Wavelength and Family Feud. The model is prompted to place the submitted clue as most people would see it, so you are aiming for the consensus reading of the spectrum and your clue.

Every player gets the same 5 rounds a day. Free, no signup, play the game then see what others submitted.

---

When we prompt Jev we can't just ask it to place the clue on the spectrum, we ask: - a score for 5 levels specifically authored for each spectrum - whether the clue is specific enough or too vague - is the clue fine to show to a general audience, is it trying to steer the evaluator, hateful, nsfw, harassing, etc.

---

There are some fun, silly little touches in the UI. Try sharing your score.

My score from today: 10/20, let me know if you beat me :)
